## Summary

- Introduces the Triage REST service — a fully automated DLQ scanner that classifies failures, creates Jira tickets for persistent errors, and requeues transient failures without human intervention
- **File-based rules and mappings**: `config/triage_rules.yaml` and `config/triage_jira_mappings.yaml` replace MySQL-backed CRUD APIs — changes go through PR, no live API management
- **Fast/slow CronJob buckets**: `fast` (ImportCallForService, every 15 min) and `slow` (all queues, hourly) replace the single global scan — concurrent per-queue scans run in parallel via the existing per-queue lock registry
- **Redis requeue tracking**: `kache` library (`git.taservs.net/rcom/common/kache`) tracks auto-requeue counts per error group; groups that fail 3+ consecutive cycles escalate to a Jira ticket rather than requeuing indefinitely
- **Per-queue purgatory windows**: configurable look-back windows in `config/triage_queue_windows.yaml` replace the hardcoded `queued_purgatory` bypass — IBR queues default to a 2h window to avoid interrupting mid-submission batches
- Closes Jira tickets via status category matching rather than hardcoded transition names (works across RMS/CS3 projects)
- Emits OTEL push metrics for scan health, queue activity, purge, requeue, and open ticket counts

## Architecture

**Scan model**
- Two CronJob buckets — both start suspended; unsuspend per-environment as queues are handed off from autoDLQ
  - `fast`: `POST /scan?queue=ImportCallForService` every 15 min (CFS ~1h SLA requires ≤18 min response time)
  - `slow`: `POST /scan` (all queues) every hour — ImportCallForService is skipped if the fast scan holds its lock
- No global scan mutex — concurrent scans of different queues are expected and allowed
- Same-queue overlap returns 409 via `QueueOpRegistry` per-queue lock

**Rules and mappings**
- `config/triage_rules.yaml` — loaded at startup via `RulesService.LoadYAML()`
- `config/triage_jira_mappings.yaml` — loaded at startup via `config.LoadTicketMappings()`
- `config/triage_queue_windows.yaml` — per-queue look-back window overrides
- REST APIs: `GET /rules`, `GET /rules/{id}/test` (debug), `GET /jira/mappings` — read-only; no CRUD

**Requeue escalation**
- Redis via `kache` (AKV secrets: `redis-axon-something-rms-host`, `redis-axon-something-rms-port`, `redis-axon-something-rms-key-1`)
- Escalation threshold: 3 consecutive auto-requeues → create ticket (configurable via `SCAN_REQUEUE_ESCALATION_THRESHOLD`)
- Graceful fallback: cache disabled if `KACHE_HOST` not configured; server starts cleanly without Redis

**Jira routing**
- Rules set a `label`; `triage_jira_mappings.yaml` maps `label → project / issue type / components / squad`
- Fallback: unknown label → `rms-integrations-oncall` RMS project with `rms-integrations-triage-routing-fallback` label
- CS notification: out of scope — handled by Jira project automation in CS3/RMS (owned by Dave Lockwood, Dylan Tantalo)

## What's pending before activating

- [ ] Confirm `KACHE_HOST` / `KACHE_PORT` / `KACHE_PASSWORD` AKV secret names match per environment
- [ ] Unsuspend `fast` and `slow` CronJobs per environment as queues are handed off from autoDLQ
- [ ] Drop `triage_rules` and `triage_jira_mappings` DB tables in DBScripts once rollback window passes

## Test plan

- [ ] `make test` — unit tests with race detector
- [ ] `make e2e-test` — full E2E suite (docker-compose with mock-jira and mock-conductor)
- [ ] Deploy to AG1 and US2; validate rules load from YAML: `GET /rules` returns expected rule set
- [ ] `POST /scan?queue=ImportCallForService&dry=true` — confirm rules fire from YAML
- [ ] Trigger fast CronJob manually; verify 409 if fired while previous run still active
- [ ] Apply `rms-integrations-triage-requeue-ready` label → trigger `POST /scan/jira` — verify requeue and Done transition
- [ ] Confirm server starts cleanly with `KACHE_HOST` unset (cache disabled path)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Detailed Behavior

### Behaviors Tested

- **Actions API** - Tests the `/actions` endpoint for orchestrated multi-step operations.
  - Executes jira-requeue action: fetches transaction IDs from a Jira ticket, requeues them via Conductor, and closes the ticket
  - Returns 400 when ticketKey is missing for jira-requeue
  - Returns 422 when the ticket has no transaction IDs attached
  - Seeds a test ticket with real transaction IDs from recent failures for a given queue
  - Returns 400 when queue is missing for seed-test-ticket
  - Returns 400 for unknown action types

- **Jira Ticket Hierarchy** - Tests the parent-child ticket structure for recurring error groups.
  - Creates a three-level hierarchy (grandparent integration → parent error-group → child monthly ticket) on first escalation
  - Reuses existing hierarchy when the same error occurs in the same month and agency
  - Creates distinct parent tickets when the same error occurs in different agencies
  - Walks parent-child relationships during jira scan to requeue all children under a released parent
  - Processes legacy flat tickets (no hierarchy) without failing

- **Escalation Threshold** - Tests automatic escalation to Jira after repeated auto-requeues.
  - Creates a ticket when requeue count reaches the configured threshold (default 3)
  - Continues auto-requeuing when below the threshold
  - Stores counts in MySQL or Redis (based on configuration) with TTL-based expiry

- **Rollover Scan** - Tests the monthly retention job that prevents partition drop data loss.
  - Emits `auto_requeue_aged_tickets_total` gauge for open parent tickets older than 60 days with age bucket labels
  - Requeues child tickets older than 10 months to refresh the 12-month retention clock
  - For batch integrations (e.g., IBR submission), labels tickets instead of requeuing and pages the owning team
  - Skips young parent tickets (under 60 days) without emitting metrics

- **Queue Operations Lock Registry** - Tests mutual exclusion for purge and other queue operations.
  - Allows first operation to acquire a queue lock
  - Returns conflict error when a second operation attempts to acquire the same locked queue
  - Permits independent locks on different queues simultaneously
  - Releases lock so the queue can be re-acquired
  - Handles concurrent acquire/release operations safely

- **Bot Comment Storage** - Tests idempotent transaction ID attachment via Jira comments.
  - Stores multiple comment updates by replacing in-place (not appending) when AttachTransactionIDs is called multiple times
  - Unions transaction IDs from multiple bot comments when reading back from a ticket

- **Scan Job Status and Locking** - Tests scan lifecycle and progress tracking.
  - Returns current scan progress including queues scanned, groups matched, and actions taken
  - Populates lastScan timestamp and stats after a scan completes
  - Returns 409 Conflict when a scan is already in progress for a queue
  - Executes dry-run scans without invoking requeue or ticket creation

- **Pause API** - Tests queue pause/unpause endpoints for manual control.
  - Marks a queue as paused so the scan loop skips it
  - Unpauses a queue to resume automatic scans
  - Both operations are idempotent (pausing twice or unpausing a non-paused queue returns 200)
  - Status endpoint reflects currently paused queues

- **Failures API** - Tests error-grouped transaction retrieval.
  - Groups transactions by normalized error message using Levenshtein similarity
  - Supports relative interval formats (2d, 30m) and ISO 8601 timestamps
  - Returns paginated results with hasMore indicator
  - Handles empty queues gracefully
  - Returns 400 for missing or invalid interval parameters

- **Configuration and Mapping** - Tests config loading and Jira label-to-project routing.
  - Loads queue windows, ticket mappings, and rules from YAML files at startup
  - Returns empty mappings (not error) when mapping file does not exist
  - Finds case-insensitive label matches in ticket mappings
  - Falls back to default routing when no explicit mapping exists
  - Resolves integration type (default/web-service/batch) from rules using exact or glob match

- **Health Checks** - Tests liveness and readiness probes.
  - Liveness probe always returns 200 OK
  - Readiness probe pings MySQL, ActiveMQ Jolokia, and escalation store (Redis or MySQL) and returns 503 if any are unavailable

- **Middleware** - Tests request ID propagation, logging, and panic recovery.
  - Propagates existing X-Request-ID header or generates a unique one
  - Logs structured request/response details including status code and duration
  - Catches panics and returns 500 Internal Server Error without crashing the server

## Summary

- Switch ci.yaml from `language: chart` to `language: go` to get the full containerize pipeline (Docker build, push, image tag stamping into values.yaml)
- Replace all `chart-*.yaml@v1` workflow templates with `go-*.yaml@v1`
- Add minimal `go.mod` and no-op build/test commands since this is a flyway-only repo with no Go source code
- Generate stub `coverage.txt` and `coverage.xml` to satisfy the Go pipeline's coverage reporting

## Why

`language: chart` skips Docker image builds and `image-tag-paths` stamping. This caused ArgoCD failures because the packaged chart had an empty image tag (`tag: ""`), producing invalid YAML. Other repos (dalor, ibrsubmissionsvc) don't hit this because they use `language: go` or `language: csharp` which runs the full containerize pipeline. DBScripts is unique — it's a standalone flyway repo with only a Dockerfile and SQL scripts.

See: [Spike doc — Blockers section](https://axon.quip.com/rMnrA61bDkjr/Spike-RMS-Integrations-GHEC-Migration)
